assessment.nobel_worthiness: Recasts intracellular organization as a physical-chemical problem: liquid-liquid phase separation of proteins and nucleic acids forms membraneless compartments (P granules, nucleoli, stress granules). From a soft-matter and self-assembly view this is a new and general organizing principle, with wide influence on cell biology, neurodegeneration (links to amyloid and aggregation) and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne established the liquid-like behaviour of P granules (2009) and the condensate concept; Rosen's multivalent-interaction and phase-diagram work gave the quantitative physical framework. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded physics and are credible alternatives, so a three-person limit forces a hard allocation.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across many systems and labs within about 15 years, and conceptually stable. Open debate continues over which in vivo assemblies are true thermodynamic phase separation versus other assemblies, so timing is mostly good but the interpretation is still being refined.
uncertainties: Physiological relevance and the exact mechanism in cells are contested for some condensates.
Fair division of credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is unresolved.
Whether the Chemistry committee would consider it chemistry rather than cell biology or physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable-lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly and colloid-design solution to delivering nucleic acids, enabling siRNA therapy (patisiran) and mRNA vaccines at global scale. Pre-existing knowledge of lipid polymorphism, pKa-dependent charge and membrane fusion was turned into an engineered medicine. Importance and impact are very large.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the foundational lipid-nanoparticle and ionizable-lipid concepts and formulation methods; Anderson's lipid-library discovery and Langer's delivery science were also important; MacLachlan and colleagues developed the SNALP/LNP products. Hope and Madden are early co-inventors. Credit is spread across academia and industry and overlaps with the 2023 mRNA prize (Kariko, Weissman).
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated by the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and an approved siRNA drug, so confirmation is strong and independent. Recognition is timely, but the nucleoside-modification prize in 2023 may be seen as having already covered the mRNA vaccine story.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize and difficulty selecting three from six or more inventors.
Patent and industry priority disputes may complicate attribution.
Share of credit between ionizable-lipid design and formulation process is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity chemistry: heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glue degraders hijack E3 ligases to degrade targets, opening previously undruggable proteins. Conceptually original, a clear new modality, and with many compounds in clinical trials. Mechanism is a chemistry of ternary-complex formation and cooperativity.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, explaining molecular glues. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later advances (VHL ligands, expansion). Credit is multi-part and the PROTAC and glue strands may need different laureates.
assessment.maturity: Early clinical data are promising (e.g. ARV-471, ARV-110 stages) but no PROTAC drug is yet widely approved, though glue degraders (lenalidomide class) are established. Possibly slightly early for the full modality.
uncertainties: Pending late-stage clinical outcomes for PROTACs.
Two distinct strands (bifunctional vs glue) with different inventors.
Proper allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another in genomic DNA without double-strand breaks, a molecular-engineering achievement building on deaminase chemistry. High clinical relevance, with first therapeutic uses of base editing, and a conceptually novel route to precise editing.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led both the cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainees; the Kondo/Nishida group independently reported a cytidine deaminase-based editor, which complicates priority. A single-laureate configuration with Liu is most defensible.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent reproduction and early human clinical results. After the 2020 CRISPR chemistry prize, a Chemistry committee may consider genome engineering recognized, but base editing is a distinct chemical advance and timing is plausible.
uncertainties: Priority relative to the Kondo and Nishida independent work.
Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with Liu's prime editing candidacy.
Long-term safety and off-target profiles still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory explain how proteins fold quickly to unique structures, and experimental phi-value analysis tested the transition states. This is a core physical-chemistry framework of statistical mechanics applied to biomolecules, with lasting influence on folding, binding and aggregation (relevant to amyloid).
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic developed the landscape theory; Fersht contributed the experimental kinetics and protein-engineering methods; Bryngelson and Dill are prominent. Allocation between theory and experiment is plausible but contested, and Dill's role in the hydrophobic and lattice models adds ambiguity.
assessment.maturity: A mature, widely validated framework now decades old. Impact of AlphaFold on structure prediction (2024 Nobel) does not replace mechanistic folding insight, but some may regard folding as partly recognized.
uncertainties: Predominantly conceptual and theoretical, with less direct experimental proof for the funnel picture.
Credit among theorists is not cleanly separable.
Possible perception that 2024 prize partly addressed protein folding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase to determine stoichiometry, subunit architecture and ligand binding, notably for membrane proteins in lipid and detergent environments where lipid-protein interactions can be resolved. A clear methodological step extending the 2002 ESI prize.
assessment.attribution: Robinson is the leading figure for intact complexes and membrane proteins; Heck and Chait made major contributions to complex analysis; Loo and Gross are credible but add allocation difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and mature. Whether the technique is distinct enough from the ESI Nobel and from the proteomics-related prizes is a question.
uncertainties: Closeness to previously recognized electrospray ionization work.
Gas-phase structural fidelity of some assemblies remains debated.
Several strong contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers enabled the fastest-rising solar cell efficiency in history, now above 25 percent, with a rich materials chemistry of defects, ion migration and composition engineering. Great scientific and societal significance.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell (2009); Park's solid-state cell (2012) and Snaith's meso-superstructured and planar devices were decisive. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel are also major contributors, so attribution is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are independently certified, but long-term operational stability and commercialization remain unproven, so recognition might be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Device stability and lead toxicity unresolved.
Crowded credit, with Grätzel's connection to dye-sensitized cells.
Physics vs chemistry framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by clonal amplification and reversible-terminator chemistry transformed biology and medicine, with reversible terminator and cluster chemistry as molecular innovations. Impact is enormous and enduring.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented the Solexa chemistry; Mayer co-developed clustering; Rothberg's pyrosequencing and Ju's work are related but separate strands, which complicates a clean prize.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and widely confirmed, with decades of impact; timing is overdue if recognized.
uncertainties: Multiple competing platforms and priority issues.
Industrial development and patent-driven attribution.
Whether committee regards it as chemistry.
